_comment: Reviewed prose stored as data — tier 2 of the three-tier rule in sources/scope.md ('No free-generated text on the site'). Each block carries a status: every tier-2 text passes through one review before flipping to 'approved', with the review date recorded in 'reviewed'; 'final' marks the masthead pair George signed off as-is. Slots in {braces} are filled at build time from gate-checked objects — never hardcoded here. The site-wide blocks resolve their slots against the site summary object (data/summaries/site.json) in web/lib/sitetext.ts; 'ego_notes' resolves its slots against the computed ego view in sources/build_ego_views.py, which bakes the rendered sentence into data/graph/ego/<file>.json.
The two lines under the logo, in the order they render.
`descriptor` is the line that sits under the wordmark on every surface that carries
one. `positioning` is the sentence that says what the platform is; it is George's
wording, reviewed, and it is locked — no surface paraphrases it, and nothing computes
a variant of it.
They were `tagline` and `subline` and said what the register did. The rename is not
cosmetic: the old pair described a decoding pipeline, and the platform's claim is now
that it connects technologies, policy, projects and capital. See amendment brief 2 §1.
masthead.descriptor: Intelligence on what Europe builds next.
masthead.positioning: Eufabric is the intelligence platform that connects Europe's industrial technologies, the policies that shape them, and the projects and capital that bring them to life.

perimeter.template: Eufabric decodes EU legislation into data. Each act is read provision by provision into individual measures: obligations, prohibitions, incentives, and rights, every one carrying the verbatim source text and a link to the official version. Measures are mapped to sectors in two ways: sectors an act names directly, and sectors it reaches through supply chains, regulatory dependencies, or procurement channels, with supply-chain reach computed from Eurostat input-output data. The measures are then aggregated per sector, so each sector page shows its full position across all legislation on the platform: what binds it directly, what reaches it indirectly, and through which channel. The platform currently holds {measures_count} measures from {acts_count} legislative acts across {sectors_count} sectors, and it grows as new legislation is adopted. Every act's verification status is stated on the coverage page. The platform does not cover national implementing measures or guidance documents, and nothing on this site is legal advice.

_comment: The launch perimeter, stated on the coverage page. George's ruling in brief 4 §1,
transcribed rather than composed: what the platform covers at launch, what it does
not, and why electricity is a parameter on every page rather than a tile of its own.
It sits beside the perimeter paragraph rather than inside it. That paragraph is
about METHOD — how an act becomes measures and how a measure reaches a sector — and
it was reviewed as such on 2026-08-18. This one is about SCOPE, it will move when
the seventh industry lands, and folding the two together would put a sentence with a
short life inside a paragraph with a long one.
launch_perimeter.paragraph: Eufabric launches narrow: Europe's energy-intensive industries and the materials they make. Six are covered at launch — cement, steel, chemicals (organic chemicals and plastics), batteries, hydrogen production including ammonia, and circular materials, meaning the recovery industry that turns used material back into feedstock. Semiconductors, automotive and defence are out of scope for launch. They are a different genre: nothing at their centre carries a carbon cost, and what they need built is capability rather than cleaner ways of making the same thing. Electricity and grids are not one of the six either. Power prices and grid connection decide what happens in all of them, so they are stated on each industry's own page rather than given a heading of their own. Every other sector listed on this page is one the legislation reaches without being one of the six.

files.ppwr: The packaging regulation's classifications are from a preliminary reading and have not yet been independently confirmed.

coverage_line.template: {acts_count} acts decoded so far; the platform grows as new legislation is adopted.

ego_notes._comment: One note per register file whose measures name and reach no sector at all. A note is REQUIRED for such a file: build_ego_views.py fails rather than composing one, because the sentence has to say what a missing sector ring means, and only a person can decide that. Slots are computed by the builder from the view it has just built — {measure_count} is the file's own measure count, {act_count} the number of distinct acts its spokes point at. Both are filled the same way; nothing in the sentence is a typed-in number.

files.omnibus: None of the omnibus's {measure_count} measures names a specific sector. The act applies horizontally, to companies across the whole economy based on size and activity. Zero named sectors means no sector-specific provisions, not zero impact. Every connection shown is one of the {act_count} acts its measures amend, cite or depend on.

record_templates._comment: One template family per legislative-event shape. Slots in {braces} are computed by sources/build_records.py from the register and the manifest and filled at build time; a slot the builder cannot compute fails the build rather than rendering empty, and a record whose event fits no family here fails the build rather than being composed. Every family carries TWO bodies: 'body', and 'body_no_reach' for an act whose reach may not be stated — an amending proposal, whose reach is computed against the proposal rather than the consolidated base it amends (sources/scope.md, 'Reach is not stated on a record about an amending proposal'). The builder drops the reach slot for such an act, so a body that mentions reach fails the build instead of rendering. Written in display vocabulary from the start, per the display-vocabulary ruling in sources/scope.md: measures and sectors, never rows or register. REVIEWED AND APPROVED 2026-08-20, after George read all four backfilled records rendered. The page layer must still refuse to render a family whose status is not 'approved': a later edit to any sentence here drops it back to draft and stops rendering until it is read again.

new_act_ingested.headline: {act_name}: {measure_count} measures now on the platform, naming {named_count} sectors

The act names {named_count} sectors in its own text — most often {top_sector}, on {top_sector_named_count} measures — and reaches {reached_count} more through supply chains, dependencies on other acts, or procurement.

amendment._comment: The verb is computed, not written: {relationship} comes from what the manifest records between the two acts — an act that repeals its predecessor replaces it, and an act that amends one amends it. PPWR is the live case for the first (sources/scope.md, 'Carry-overs come from repeal, not from amendment'), and a family template that hardcoded 'amended' would state the wrong relationship on its first record.

These measures name {named_count} sectors — most often {top_sector}, on {top_sector_named_count} of them — and reach {reached_count} more through supply chains, dependencies on other acts, or procurement.

They name {named_count} sectors — most often {top_sector}, on {top_sector_named_count} of them — and reach {reached_count} more through supply chains, dependencies on other acts, or procurement.

status_change.body: {act_name} is no longer a proposal. Its {measure_count} measures are adopted law. They name {named_count} sectors — most often {top_sector}, on {top_sector_named_count} of them — and reach {reached_count} more through supply chains, dependencies on other acts, or procurement.
status_change.body_no_reach: {act_name} is no longer a proposal. Its {measure_count} measures are adopted law. They name {named_count} sectors — most often {top_sector}, on {top_sector_named_count} of them.

status_notes._comment: Appended to every record body, chosen by the legal standing of the act the record is about — the same STATUS_RULE the findings gate applies. A record about a proposal has to say so on its own face: the record is permanent and will outlive the proposal.
status_notes.adopted: This act is adopted. It is law, not a proposal.
status_notes.proposed: This is a Commission proposal, {com}, under procedure {procedure}. It is not law yet, and it can change before it is.
status_notes.mixed: The proposal {com}, under procedure {procedure}, would change an act already in force. What it adds is not law yet; the act it changes is.

cement.sentence: European cement is under one transition, decarbonisation, and it turns on a fact no energy choice can reach: most of a kiln's CO2 comes out of the limestone rather than the fuel, which is why the sector's future runs through capture, the pipes and stores that capture depends on, and whoever is willing to pay for the result.

_comment: One reviewed paragraph per sector that has a transition map: the orientation a reader
needs before the page's own numbers mean anything. Tier 2 of the three-tier rule in
sources/scope.md — reviewed prose stored as data, never generated, never per-page free
text.
IT SITS ABOVE THE COMPUTED LEAD AND REPLACES NOTHING. The lead block below it is
unchanged and still computed from the panels; this paragraph is the standing context
that does not move when the data does, which is exactly why it is written once and
reviewed rather than templated.
FOUR BEATS, THE SAME ORDER EVERY TIME, so a reader who has read one sector can read any
other: what the sector is and its weight in Europe; why decarbonising it is structurally
hard; the technology paths; how EU policy frames it. It closes on the question the
page's data answers, so the handoff into the detail below is deliberate.
NEARLY NUMBER-FREE ON PURPOSE. Every figure on this site carries a source link and an
as-of date (§0.1 of eufabric-page-specifications.md). A number in standing prose would
need both and would go stale silently, and the sourced figures are one line further down
the page in any case.
While the status is `draft` nothing here renders and the page opens on the lead block as
before. sources/check_sector_schema.py fails for a mapped sector with no paragraph and
prints the drafts on every run.

cement.paragraph: Cement is the binding agent of the built environment. Concrete is the most used man-made material on earth, and European construction depends on a domestic industry that operates on thin margins with high energy and carbon intensity. Most of the sector's emissions come not from burning fuel but from the chemistry of clinker, the limestone-derived core of cement, which releases CO2 as it is processed. That makes cement one of the hardest sectors to decarbonise: efficiency and clean electricity cannot remove process emissions, so the transition runs through carbon capture, clinker substitution and alternative fuels. EU policy treats it accordingly: carbon pricing raises the cost of conventional production, a border adjustment shields producers from unpriced imports, and public funding underwrites the first capture projects. The open question is who pays for low-carbon cement while it costs more than conventional supply.

_comment: THE TWO NAME SLOTS, brief 5 §2.1. Every heading on a sector page is a
template, and a template needs the sector's name in two grammatical shapes:
short   the bare noun, used inside a sentence — 'cement', 'circular
materials'. Never carries 'European': the templates that want it
say it themselves, which is why the projects heading reads 'in
European {short}' and the feed heading reads 'in {short}'.
phrase  the full noun phrase for a heading about the sector as a whole —
'the European cement industry'. Lower case as stored; the
renderer capitalises the first letter only where the slot OPENS a
heading, which no template does today.
KEYED ON ECOSYSTEM ID, NOT SECTOR SLUG. The keys are the six instances in
data/transition/ecosystems.json. The chemicals ecosystem spans two FIGARO
slugs (chem, chem/plastics) and batteries covers part of one (batsol), so a
slug-keyed store would have to say the chemicals name twice and would have no
key at all for hydrogen or circular materials. web/lib/ecosystems.ts resolves
a sector slug to its instance; a slug that belongs to no instance has no
name slots and cannot render the template, which is a build failure rather
than a fallback.
BOTH SLOTS ARE REQUIRED for all six, and sources/check_h2_templates.py fails
the build on an empty one. Unlike the ecosystem descriptions these are not
optional prose a surface can omit — a heading with an unfilled slot is not a
heading.
THE FIXED SEQUENCE, brief 5 §2. The sector page answers the same questions in
the same order on every sector, so the interface is learned once. The order of
the `sections` array below IS the render order and the nav order —
sources/check_section_order.py reads this array and fails the build if the
template disagrees with it.
EVERY HEADING IS A QUESTION, and every question is stored here rather than
written in the component, so the wording is reviewable in one place and cannot
drift between sectors. Slots are {short} and {phrase} from sector_names above.
A SECTION WITH NO DATA IS OMITTED, from the page and from the nav both — brief
5 §2, which amends the fixed-presence rule in page specifications §0.5 for
this page type. An empty section is not rendered with a 'none tracked' line
here: nine sections of which four say nothing is a worse page than five that
say something. Which sections have data is a question for the data, not for
this file, so no entry below is marked optional.
NOT IN THE LIST. The lead block, which opens the page with no H2 and is
excluded from the nav (row 0). Sources, which page specifications §0.5 makes
the final section of every sector page and which brief 5 §2 does not number —
it renders last, unnumbered, outside the nav, on the same footing as the lead
block, and §2 is amended to say so in step 6.
sector_sections.h1_comment: `phrase` is deliberately not used in the H1: it already carries 'European', and 'The European cement industry in Europe's industrial transition' says Europe twice.

What EU rules and money support in {short}

_comment: THE REGENERATED LEAD, HELD FOR REVIEW — brief 4 §6, step 2.
What the sector page actually renders is the BUILT lead in

IT IS NOT A SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH AND MUST NOT BECOME ONE. Nothing in web/ reads

cement.sentence: European cement is decarbonising by capturing the CO2 its kilns emit, and the main question is who pays for it.
cement.why_it_matters: Cement made this way costs more than the cement it replaces, so whether Europe gets it depends on who covers the difference.

facts.text: Low-carbon cement costs 75-150% above a conventional plant to make, on the International Energy Agency's figures.
8 European cement projects are under way, and 4 of them have taken a final investment decision.
Importers of cement pay for the carbon in what they bring into Europe, currently €75.46 per tonne.
Slite CCS was paused on 19 November 2025.

_comment: One reviewed description per ecosystem instance — page specifications §4.2. Two
sentences: what the ecosystem contains, and where its boundary runs. The boundaries
are the whole point of the block — that chemicals excludes fertilisers, that ammonia
is read under hydrogen, that batteries does not mean solar — and none of them can be
computed from the edges, because a boundary is a decision rather than a fact about
the data.
WHERE IT RENDERS: the coverage page, and the tile's hover text. NEVER on the tile
face (§4.2): the tile carries the name and the icon, and a paragraph on it would be
the perimeter argument competing with the six names the grid exists to present.
EMPTY UNTIL GEORGE SUPPLIES THE TEXT. The slot, the getter and the gate are built;
the words are not written here. web/lib/sitetext.ts returns null for an empty or
unreviewed entry, and every surface renders nothing rather than a placeholder — the
same discipline as the orientation paragraph. sources/check_sector_schema.py lists
which instances are still outstanding on every run.
